note: Level 1, both label levels read (.sav copied from the batch_659 wallace_2026_s2_engage cache; sha256 matches; the Study 2 .sps contains no like text). CODE DERIVATION: SINGLE spec s2_like.csv = (s2, like{i} -> like{i}, i = 1,2), no flip, so item IS the source column name: exempt from Step 5b, no verification files. Study 2 only (live has no cov_study and no itemcov_recoded column). Variable labels: like1 = I would like this professor., like2 = I would view this professor positively. -- shipped verbatim, unprefixed (single study). OPTIONS: both items value-labelled 1=1 - Strongly agree, 2..6 bare digits, 7=7 - Strongly disagree; shipped Strongly agree / Strongly disagree with the number prefixes stripped (sibling convention), 2-6 blank, not padded. Sanity counts (not required for the exemption): source 838 rows, 838 non-missing on each item; live 1676 rows = 838 ids x 2; item resp-count vectors source = live exactly: like1 112/96/87/145/132/144/122, like2 125/94/93/109/129/158/130; every item used all 7 levels. Direction cross-check: like mean correlates -0.46 with the Study 2 interest mean (interest1-3, labelled 1 = not at all ... 7 = extremely) and +0.67 with the engage1-2 mean (1 = Strongly agree), r(like1, like2) = +0.93, so the printed 1 = Strongly agree direction is consistent with the data; high resp = LESS liking, as the build script docstring states. No instructions or lead-in text in the .sav or .sps; instructions left blank. Dictionary Description says instructor; the .sav wording says professor, shipped as labelled. Rights: study-authored items; no fee, permission, NC or redistribution clause located (silence = permission). Not in instrument_rights_register.csv; no register row written.
public_note: Responses run 1 = Strongly agree to 7 = Strongly disagree, so a higher value means less liking of the professor.
